samples.title: Smooth gradient
samples.description: A grayscale ramp that brightens from top-left to bottom-right.
samples.why: Every entry is a linear function of (row, column), so the matrix has rank 2: two singular components rebuild it almost exactly.

samples.title: Checkerboard
samples.description: An 8 x 8 board of black and white squares.
samples.why: Repeated structure means low rank: the board is exactly rank 2 (a +/- pattern outer-multiplied by another), despite its hard edges.

samples.title: Geometric shapes
samples.description: A circle, a rectangle and a triangle on a shaded background.
samples.why: Axis-aligned blocks are cheap; diagonals and curves need more components, so you can watch the edges sharpen as k grows.

samples.title: Edge-heavy pattern
samples.description: Diagonal stripes, a grid and concentric rings.
samples.why: Diagonal and circular edges are not aligned with rows and columns, so the singular values decay slowly.

samples.title: Low-rank construction
samples.description: A 256 x 192 image: four separable cosine patterns plus a constant brightness offset.
samples.why: Before 8-bit rounding the rank is exactly 5: the spectrum drops to rounding-noise level after sigma_5, and k = 5 is already nearly perfect.

samples.title: Complex texture
samples.description: Fractal 1/f noise with detail at every scale.
samples.why: Nothing here is low rank. The spectrum decays slowly, which shows where truncated SVD stops being a good compressor.

samples.title: Tiny 16 x 16 face
samples.description: A 16 x 16 pixel face, small enough to print the whole matrix.
samples.why: Small enough for the exact SVD in a blink, and the pixel-to-matrix correspondence can be read entry by entry.

samples.title: Photograph (grayscale)
samples.description: NASA's portrait of astronaut Eileen Collins (public domain), converted to luminance, 256 x 256.
samples.why: A natural image: a few components capture the large light/dark layout, and fine detail arrives slowly.

samples.title: Photograph (colour)
samples.description: The same public-domain NASA portrait in RGB, 256 x 256.
samples.why: Colour means three matrices (R, G, B) decomposed separately, so the storage count is three times larger.
